provenance_note: The five outcomes here are transcribed from PLAN.md §5.4 ('Regulatory leg, K=5'), which grounds them in the live IMO negotiating positions as of the current round (PLAN.md §11.2 item 15 flags this as the fastest-moving item in the document — re-check immediately before submission). This is the fixed K=5 the tensor's regulatory leg `r` (§3.1) indexes over; Phase 3 consumes this file rather than redefining the scenario set.
price_axis_treatment_note: Per PLAN.md §3.6(b): a two-tier proposal is placed on the effective-marginal-carbon-price axis as a tier-annotated range, never collapsed to a single point; a proposal with no posted price at all is a qualitative marker with its placement assumption stated explicitly; a scenario with no NZF at all requires the CII/FuelEU implied-price converter (implied_price.py) rather than a direct NZF tier read.

scenarios.label: Liberia-style
scenarios.description: Transferable surplus units largely replacing the fund mechanism
scenarios.notes: A market-design proposal, not a tariff (PLAN.md §3.6b) — no posted price exists to place on the axis. Any placement must state its assumption explicitly next to the tick mark, not bake it silently into a number.

scenarios.label: Tuvalu-style
scenarios.notes: PLAN.md gives only the Tier 1 figure for this proposal; tier_2 is null here rather than guessed.

scenarios.label: Brazil-style
scenarios.notes: This is a reduction-percentage schedule, not a posted per-tonne price — it needs the same implied-price treatment as scenario 5, not a direct tier read.

scenarios.label: Adoption fails again
scenarios.description: CII, FuelEU, and EU ETS only, no NZF
scenarios.notes: PLAN.md §3.6(b): 'does not mean zero carbon price' — placing this on the same axis as the other four requires the implied-price converter (implied_price.py) applied to CII's corrective-action consequence and FuelEU's penalty formula. Any claim about whether this stack crosses a given switching point is provisional until that converter is run (PLAN.md §3.6(b)).
